title: High-Pass Filter - WiFi 5 GHz for GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Mei-Ling Chen

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a High-Pass Filter filter targeting WiFi 5 GHz for GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter. The filter is designed on AlN on SiC substrate with a target center frequency of 749.5 MHz and bandwidth of 381.9 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: High-Pass Filter
- Frequency Band: WiFi 5 GHz
- Application: GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter
- Substrate: AlN on SiC
- Package: Fan-Out WLP
- Design Tool: Keysight ADS 2024
- Design Center: Andover HQ Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the High-Pass Filter design targeting WiFi 5 GHz. Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       749.5 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       381.9 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 3.3 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 20.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 50.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 27.0 dB
Q Factor:               1759
Temperature Coefficient:-13.1 ppm/°C
Die Size:               1.1 x 0.6 mm
Wafer Size:             8-inch
Number of Resonators:   10
Electrode Material:     Pt/Al
Passivation:            SiO2/Si3N4 stack
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Keysight ADS 2024 and load the High-Pass Filter template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: AlN on SiC with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 749.5 MHz, BW 381.9 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 3.3 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (Fan-Out WLP).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (8-inch, AlN on SiC).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Keysight E5080B ENA.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 2248 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 3.3 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 20.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 573 MHz offset >= 50.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 2 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 1.2 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +32 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 500 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 97%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2025-01-06
Devices Tested:         43
Insertion Loss (meas):  3.02 dB
Return Loss (meas):     22.3 dB
Rejection (meas):       52.8 dB
Isolation (meas):       32.4 dB
Q Factor (meas):        1759
Group Delay Variation:  5.3 ns
Power Handling:         +27 dBm
Die Yield:              94.7%

Result Classification:  NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The High-Pass Filter design demonstrated below-target performance for WiFi 5 GHz.
b) Insertion loss is marginally above target; electrode thickness optimization recommended.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Slight frequency drift observed at +85°C; TC layer thickness may need adjustment.
e) Batch-to-batch reproducibility confirmed over 3 wafer lots.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
